messages:
andrea: Heads-up — nightly eval (prompt correctness suite) dropped for the contract_summaries promptset on candidate model rwd-gptx-3a. Pass rate fell from 97.6% -> 82.1% overnight. :rotating_light:
eval-bot: run_id=nightly-176235, suite=prompt_correctness, model=rwd-gptx-3a, pass_rate=0.821, fail_count=48/270, top_fail_types=[truncated_output, hallucinated_entities, malformed_json]
sam: Oof. Is this the quantized candidate or a float baseline?
mike: It's the new quantized bring-up (int8+groupwise) that also swapped in tokenizer v2. Small change in tokenizer mapping for the <list_item> placeholder. That stood out in the model onboarding diff.
katie: Reproduced locally on a seed subset. Example failure: prompt asks "List the parties in the contract" and candidate returns "Parties: CorpX, \uFFFD" — there's a stray replacement char followed by cutoff. Looks like tokenization is inserting an unknown token mid-list which kills the decode.
andrea: That fits truncated_output + malformed_json. Which commit introduced tokenizer v2? Link?
mike: https://git.redwood/repo/tokenizer/compare/refs/heads/main...tokenizer/v2 — small remap for control tokens to optimize packing. Intended to shrink vocab but new mapping collided with the sentinel we use for list boundaries.
sam: So root cause hypothesis = tokenizer remap changed sentinel token ids, causing KV-cache alignment mismatch in quant path -> early termination / decode corruption on list-heavy prompts.
katie: Quick repro snippet I used:
```
# reproduce
nightly_eval --suite prompt_correctness --promptset contract_summaries --model rwd-gptx-3a --seed 42 --limit 50
# inspect tokenization
python -c "from tokenizer import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer('v2').encode('<<LIST>> Party1, Party2'))"
```
results show sentinel id 972 -> 13 (v1->v2 mapping) for the same string.
andrea: Immediate actions: 1) Roll canary off candidate. 2) Revert tokenizer mapping in the quant pipeline until we have gated tests. 3) Add a gating rule to nightly bring-up: contract_summaries pass_rate >= 95% AND no malformed_json regressions. 4) Create an A/B canary run with token-level diffs to catch sentinel remaps.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: deploy_group=dedicated-canary, from=rwd-gptx-3a to=rwd-gptx-3 (stable) — ETA 2m.
mike: I'll open a revert PR for tokenizer/v2 in the quant pipeline and tag @katie for unit tests. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/5582
katie: I'll add unit tests in tokenizers/tests/test_sentinels.py that assert sentinel ids match v1 mapping and hook into the nightly preflight. Also adding an integration that runs on 100 contract_summaries prompts with deterministic seeds.
sam: For medium-term: we should add a tokenizer compatibility check to model onboarding: when tokenizer mapping changes, run a diff on sentinel tokens and fail onboarding unless explicit opt-in. Add to gates: "tokenizer_id_changes -> block".
andrea: Agreed. Also adding a quick mitigation: update the bring-up checklist to require running the decoder-smoke test (100 prompts from each critical promptset) before enabling canary traffic. I'll file the tickets and owners below.
andrea: Tickets:
- ML-1287 revert tokenizer v2 in quant pipeline (owner: mike)
- ML-1288 add sentinel unit tests + integration (owner: katie)
- ML-1289 add tokenizer compatibility gate to onboarding (owner: sam)
- ML-1290 add contract_summaries gating rule on nightly (owner: andrea)

mike: Noted, starting revert PR now. Will post when CI green.
katie: Tests coming in this afternoon, will link branch.
andrea: Thanks all. Leaving canary offline until we have the revert + tests in place. We'll re-run nightly after merge and validate before re-enabling. :white_check_mark:
